title: Canada is taking an outsized role in the construction of the post-American world
excerpt: Carney is emulating earlier Liberals, such as Lester Pearson and Louis St. Laurent
content_html:
Annual gatherings of the great democracies in the age of Donald Trump have acquired a certain … rhythm. There is the meeting that takes place before the President arrives, when all is as it usually is between world leaders of the same broad ideological hue: convivial open sessions, chummy photo-ops, urgent side-conferences.

Then there is what happens after he gets there, and the desperate scramble to reconcile the chaos that ensues with the serene normalcy that went before: to insist that the torrent of lunacies foaming out of the President’s mouth from the moment of his arrival, making hash of everything the other conferees had agreed upon – not to mention decades of settled international law – were in fact in perfect harmony with the rest.

This year’s NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, was no different. The meeting had been intended to be a carefully staged show of support for Ukraine in the war with Russia, coupled with an equally carefully staged display of Europe’s commitment to its own defence, all in the service of proving to Mr. Trump that the bargain struck at NATO’s 2025 meeting in The Hague – higher non-U.S. defence spending in return for continued U.S. engagement in Europe – was actually being implemented.

Opinion: Was the NATO summit a success? It depends on how you define it

Then Mr. Trump arrived. He had been attacking and ridiculing NATO, and individual NATO leaders, for months prior to the summit, particularly over their failure to involve themselves in the Iran war – a debacle that has nothing to do with NATO or its core mandate. At the summit things escalated. Mr. Trump revived his demands to be given Greenland, called for a boycott on trade with Spain, and threatened to withdraw all U.S. troops from Europe, on his way to redeclaring war on Iran.

But by the time it was over all was supposedly sweetness and light. The post-conference declaration insisted on the alliance members’ “ironclad” commitment to defend each other under Article 5 of NATO’s founding treaty, mentioned “the long-term threat Russia poses,” boasted that European allies and Canada had increased spending on core defence requirements by US$139-billion last year, and pledged the allies’ “unwavering support for Ukraine.”

Mr. Trump, for his part, seemed pleased, not least by the flattery the other leaders laid on him, which he interpreted as love. “They said, ‘We love, sir, we love you.’ These are grown people saying that, isn’t that nice? … I’ve never seen anything like it. Every one of those countries, they love us, they love each other.” Whatever it was, it seemed to work. Mr. Trump even promised to license Ukraine to make U.S. Patriot air defence systems.

Of course, at most NATO summits, it would not be news that Article 5 was still intact, that the U.S. was still in it, or that the alliance viewed Russia as a threat. But that was before Mr. Trump came onto the world scene. The meeting might have succeeded in papering over the deep cracks in the alliance, but no one takes seriously Mr. Trump’s commitments, such as they are. The test of Article 5 is not what NATO partners say about it now, but what they do in the event of an attack.

Prime Minister Mark Carney says President Donald Trump arrived at NATO in a good mood and the alliance is shifting military budget burdens away from the U.S.

The Canadian Press

To say that there is now profound doubt about the United States’ willingness to defend its allies is to understate things considerably. To say that there is almost complete certainty in NATO circles that it would not is still to understate matters. The most recent, and serious, threat to the territorial integrity of a NATO member, after all, did not come from Russia. It came, and comes, from the United States: over Greenland. And it lingers still over Canada.

The Wall Street Journal this week revived controversy over a conversation first reported last year, in which Mr. Trump had allegedly threatened, in a phone call with Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, to abrogate the Treaty of 1908, defining the border between the United States and Canada. “I tear that up and your whole country unravels,” Mr. Trump reportedly told Mr. Trudeau.

However much Mr. Trump’s belligerence may have changed relations with the rest of NATO, it is nothing compared to how it has transformed relations with Canada – and changed Canada with it. Never, since 1867, have we had to take seriously the prospect that the President of the United States might attempt to seize a part of our territory, by one means or another.

Quite the opposite. The United States became our benefactor: our largest trading partner, closest ally, and military protector. No major democracy is more dependent on another country for trade, nor does any other depend as much on another for its defence.

That Canada combines both is a measure not just of how much we had come to rely on the United States, but how uniquely ill-prepared we are for the world we are now in – a world in which we not only cannot rely on the United States for our defence, but must prepare to defend ourselves from it.

And yet, it must be said, there are opportunities for Canada in this world. Sheltering within the U.S. trade and defence orbit had many benefits – assured access to U.S. markets, security from external aggression – but also infantilized us in many ways.

It convinced us, not only that we did not have to pay for our own defence, but that we had no need to defend ourselves – that we had no natural predators. It dulled our competitive edge, leading us to neglect our sputtering productivity – why concern ourselves with such things, when we could always ship our commodities south?

It allowed us to indulge in self-destructive behaviour like imposing hundreds of interprovincial trade barriers on ourselves, or indulging periodic threats of secession from one province or another. It permitted us to rely on tenuous east-west transportation and communications links that left us more vulnerable than we might have been, had we had to take seriously the threat of sabotage or other coercive measures.

And it encouraged us in that most Canadian of pastimes, preaching to others about matters that do not directly concern us, based on claims to superior virtue we have not earned – a particular irritant when it came to our notorious NATO freeloading, but a tendency to preen that had more generally consigned us to the sidelines of international affairs.

All of this is about to change – is changing already. We have been forced to change course on any number of fronts at the same time, the most radical reappraisal of our prospects and direction in at least the last 40 years, maybe since 1945 – maybe ever.

Trump has ‘won the argument’ on NATO defence spending, Carney says at summit

At one go, we are attempting to redirect some of our trade to other nations besides the U.S., including by a series of sweeping free trade agreements, while raising our defence spending to levels, whether in proportion to our GDP or to total government spending, not seen since the early 1960s.

At the same time, we are embarked upon a massive infrastructure spree, again of a kind not seen in decades: pipelines and electricity links and railways and more. Rather less has been done as yet on the productivity or internal trade barriers fronts, but these will surely have to follow – there is no way we will be able to pay for all this other spending if we don’t.

And we are beginning to be taken seriously again in international councils. Mark Carney’s personal reputation, as a former central banker and international financier, is only part of this. The reason his speech at Davos, calling on middle powers to get out from under the “hegemons’” thumbs, landed with such enormous impact was not just who said it, or where, or when – at the height of the Greenland fiasco – but that it was a Prime Minister of Canada, of all places, saying it.

This wasn’t Canada preaching from the sidelines. This was a politician with skin in the game, leading a country that was more dependent on one particular hegemon than any of the others represented there – and therefore more at risk. As a consequence, we are taking an outsized role in the construction of a post-American world.

Perhaps the most startling, and sudden, transformation has been our approach to energy development. The Prime Minister’s remarkable “forward guidance” video the other day amounted to a blunt disavowal of the last 10 years of Liberal policy. His reasoning was simple. The world has changed. New threats crowd upon us, that were not anticipated a decade ago, and new priorities must take their place alongside the fight against climate change. Government is about triage.

But it isn’t only Justin Trudeau’s legacy Mr. Carney has been busy overturning, for good or ill. It’s Pierre Trudeau’s. Mr. Carney is in many ways a throwback to a pre-Trudeau kind of Liberal. In style and tone, but even more in policy, he recalls the Liberals of the Lester Pearson era, and even more that of Louis St. Laurent: sober, bankerly, business-oriented, pro-development and pro-military.

We remember Pearson as the father of peacekeeping. We are less likely to remember him as the Cold Warrior who accepted nuclear missiles on Canadian soil, and who spent more than 3 per cent of GDP, on average, on defence.

It was the Diefenbaker Conservatives who objected to the missiles. At the time the Liberals were the continentalists of Canadian politics, seeing engagement with the U.S. as a necessary counterbalance to the imperial connection they were so anxious to be rid of. The Tories were the opposite: fond of the mother country, suspicious of the Yanks. Only much later did the roles reverse, after Britain ceased to be an issue.

Mr. Carney is a continentalist, too – he just has a different continent in mind. But his ardent pursuit of the European connection is in the same counter-balancing mould, not only of Liberal leaders past, but of statesmen through the ages: calling the Old World back into our existence, to redress the balance of the New.

sentences.zh: 英国首相马克·卡尼表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统心情愉快地抵达北约，该联盟正在将军事预算负担从美国手中转移出去。

blocks.html_en: The Canadian Press

sentences.en: The Canadian Press
sentences.zh: 加拿大新闻社

blocks.html_en: To say that there is now profound doubt about the United States’ willingness to defend its allies is to understate things considerably. To say that there is almost complete certainty in NATO circles that it would not is still to understate matters. The most recent, and serious, threat to the territorial integrity of a NATO member, after all, did not come from Russia. It came, and comes, from the United States: over Greenland. And it lingers still over Canada.

sentences.en: To say that there is now profound doubt about the United States’ willingness to defend its allies is to understate things considerably.
sentences.zh: 如果说现在人们对美国保卫其盟友的意愿存在深刻怀疑，那就太轻描淡写了。

sentences.en: To say that there is almost complete certainty in NATO circles that it would not is still to understate matters.
sentences.zh: 如果说北约内部几乎完全肯定不会这样做，那仍然是轻描淡写。

sentences.en: The most recent, and serious, threat to the territorial integrity of a NATO member, after all, did not come from Russia.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，最近对北约成员国领土完整的严重威胁并非来自俄罗斯。

sentences.en: It came, and comes, from the United States: over Greenland.
sentences.zh: 它来自美国，而且来自美国：越过格陵兰岛。

sentences.en: And it lingers still over Canada.
sentences.zh: 它仍然徘徊在加拿大上空。

blocks.html_en: The Wall Street Journal this week revived controversy over a conversation first reported last year, in which Mr. Trump had allegedly threatened, in a phone call with Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, to abrogate the Treaty of 1908, defining the border between the United States and Canada. “I tear that up and your whole country unravels,” Mr. Trump reportedly told Mr. Trudeau.

sentences.en: The Wall Street Journal this week revived controversy over a conversation first reported last year, in which Mr. Trump had allegedly threatened, in a phone call with Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, to abrogate the Treaty of 1908, defining the border between the United States and Canada.
sentences.zh: 《华尔街日报》本周再次引发了对去年首次报道的一次对话的争议，据称特朗普在与总理贾斯汀·特鲁多的电话中威胁要废除界定美国和加拿大边界的 1908 年条约。

sentences.en: “I tear that up and your whole country unravels,” Mr. Trump reportedly told Mr. Trudeau.
sentences.zh: 据报道，特朗普告诉特鲁多：“我把它撕了，你的整个国家就会崩溃。”

blocks.html_en: However much Mr. Trump’s belligerence may have changed relations with the rest of NATO, it is nothing compared to how it has transformed relations with Canada – and changed Canada with it. Never, since 1867, have we had to take seriously the prospect that the President of the United States might attempt to seize a part of our territory, by one means or another.

sentences.en: However much Mr. Trump’s belligerence may have changed relations with the rest of NATO, it is nothing compared to how it has transformed relations with Canada – and changed Canada with it.
sentences.zh: 无论特朗普的好战性可能在多大程度上改变了与北约其他国家的关系，但与它改变与加拿大的关系并随之改变加拿大的关系相比，这根本算不了什么。

sentences.en: Never, since 1867, have we had to take seriously the prospect that the President of the United States might attempt to seize a part of our territory, by one means or another.
sentences.zh: 自 1867 年以来，我们从未认真考虑过美国总统可能试图以某种方式夺取我们部分领土的前景。

blocks.html_en: Quite the opposite. The United States became our benefactor: our largest trading partner, closest ally, and military protector. No major democracy is more dependent on another country for trade, nor does any other depend as much on another for its defence.

sentences.en: Quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反。

sentences.en: The United States became our benefactor: our largest trading partner, closest ally, and military protector.
sentences.zh: 美国成为我们的恩人：我们最大的贸易伙伴、最亲密的盟友和军事保护者。

sentences.en: No major democracy is more dependent on another country for trade, nor does any other depend as much on another for its defence.
sentences.zh: 没有任何一个主要民主国家在贸易方面比另一个国家更加依赖，也没有任何其他国家在国防方面如此依赖另一个国家。

blocks.html_en: That Canada combines both is a measure not just of how much we had come to rely on the United States, but how uniquely ill-prepared we are for the world we are now in – a world in which we not only cannot rely on the United States for our defence, but must prepare to defend ourselves from it.

sentences.en: That Canada combines both is a measure not just of how much we had come to rely on the United States, but how uniquely ill-prepared we are for the world we are now in – a world in which we not only cannot rely on the United States for our defence, but must prepare to defend ourselves from it.
sentences.zh: 加拿大将两者结合起来，不仅衡量了我们对美国的依赖程度，而且还衡量了我们对现在所处的世界准备得多么不足——在这个世界中，我们不仅不能依赖美国进行国防，而且必须准备好保护自己免受美国的侵害。

sentences.en: U.S. President Donald Trump and Mr. Carney attend a meeting of the North Atlantic Council during the NATO leaders' summit.Yves Herman/Reuters
sentences.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和卡尼先生在北约领导人峰会期间出席北大西洋理事会会议。Yves Herman/Reuters

blocks.html_en: U.S. President Donald Trump and Mr. Carney attend a meeting of the North Atlantic Council during the NATO leaders' summit.Yves Herman/Reuters

sentences.en: U.S. President Donald Trump and Mr. Carney attend a meeting of the North Atlantic Council during the NATO leaders' summit.Yves Herman/Reuters
sentences.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和卡尼先生在北约领导人峰会期间出席北大西洋理事会会议。Yves Herman/Reuters

blocks.html_en: And yet, it must be said, there are opportunities for Canada in this world. Sheltering within the U.S. trade and defence orbit had many benefits – assured access to U.S. markets, security from external aggression – but also infantilized us in many ways.

sentences.en: And yet, it must be said, there are opportunities for Canada in this world.
sentences.zh: 然而，必须说的是，加拿大在这个世界上也有机会。

sentences.en: Sheltering within the U.S. trade and defence orbit had many benefits – assured access to U.S. markets, security from external aggression – but also infantilized us in many ways.
sentences.zh: 躲藏在美国贸易和国防轨道内有很多好处——确保进入美国市场、免受外部侵略——但也在很多方面让我们变得幼稚。

blocks.html_en: It convinced us, not only that we did not have to pay for our own defence, but that we had no need to defend ourselves – that we had no natural predators. It dulled our competitive edge, leading us to neglect our sputtering productivity – why concern ourselves with such things, when we could always ship our commodities south?

sentences.en: It convinced us, not only that we did not have to pay for our own defence, but that we had no need to defend ourselves – that we had no natural predators.
sentences.zh: 它让我们相信，我们不仅不需要为自己的防御付出代价，而且我们没有必要保卫自己——我们没有天敌。

sentences.en: It dulled our competitive edge, leading us to neglect our sputtering productivity – why concern ourselves with such things, when we could always ship our commodities south?
sentences.zh: 它削弱了我们的竞争优势，导致我们忽视了我们的生产力——当我们总能把商品运往南方时，为什么要关心这些事情呢？

blocks.html_en: It allowed us to indulge in self-destructive behaviour like imposing hundreds of interprovincial trade barriers on ourselves, or indulging periodic threats of secession from one province or another. It permitted us to rely on tenuous east-west transportation and communications links that left us more vulnerable than we might have been, had we had to take seriously the threat of sabotage or other coercive measures.

sentences.en: It allowed us to indulge in self-destructive behaviour like imposing hundreds of interprovincial trade barriers on ourselves, or indulging periodic threats of secession from one province or another.
sentences.zh: 它让我们沉迷于自我毁灭的行为，比如对自己施加数百个省际贸易壁垒，或者沉溺于从一个或另一个省分裂的周期性威胁。

sentences.en: It permitted us to rely on tenuous east-west transportation and communications links that left us more vulnerable than we might have been, had we had to take seriously the threat of sabotage or other coercive measures.
sentences.zh: 它使我们能够依赖脆弱的东西向交通和通讯联系，这使我们比我们必须认真对待破坏或其他强制性措施的威胁更容易受到伤害。

blocks.html_en: And it encouraged us in that most Canadian of pastimes, preaching to others about matters that do not directly concern us, based on claims to superior virtue we have not earned – a particular irritant when it came to our notorious NATO freeloading, but a tendency to preen that had more generally consigned us to the sidelines of international affairs.

sentences.en: And it encouraged us in that most Canadian of pastimes, preaching to others about matters that do not directly concern us, based on claims to superior virtue we have not earned – a particular irritant when it came to our notorious NATO freeloading, but a tendency to preen that had more generally consigned us to the sidelines of international affairs.
sentences.zh: 它鼓励了我们大多数加拿大人的消遣，向他人宣讲与我们没有直接关系的事情，基于我们没有赢得的优越美德的主张——当涉及到我们臭名昭著的北约贪图便宜时，这尤其令人恼火，但更普遍的是，这种自命不凡的倾向使我们被置于国际事务的边缘。

blocks.html_en: All of this is about to change – is changing already. We have been forced to change course on any number of fronts at the same time, the most radical reappraisal of our prospects and direction in at least the last 40 years, maybe since 1945 – maybe ever.

sentences.en: All of this is about to change – is changing already.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都即将改变——已经在改变。

sentences.en: We have been forced to change course on any number of fronts at the same time, the most radical reappraisal of our prospects and direction in at least the last 40 years, maybe since 1945 – maybe ever.
sentences.zh: 我们被迫同时在许多方面改变方向，这是至少过去 40 年来（也许是自 1945 年以来，也许是有史以来）对我们的前景和方向最彻底的重新评估。

blocks.html_en: Trump has ‘won the argument’ on NATO defence spending, Carney says at summit

sentences.en: Trump has ‘won the argument’ on NATO defence spending, Carney says at summit
sentences.zh: 卡尼在峰会上表示，特朗普在北约国防开支问题上“赢得了争论”

blocks.html_en: At one go, we are attempting to redirect some of our trade to other nations besides the U.S., including by a series of sweeping free trade agreements, while raising our defence spending to levels, whether in proportion to our GDP or to total government spending, not seen since the early 1960s.

sentences.en: At one go, we are attempting to redirect some of our trade to other nations besides the U.S., including by a series of sweeping free trade agreements, while raising our defence spending to levels, whether in proportion to our GDP or to total government spending, not seen since the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图将我们的部分贸易转向美国以外的其他国家，包括通过一系列全面的自由贸易协定，同时将我们的国防开支提高到自 1960 年代初以来未见的水平，无论是占 GDP 的比例还是占政府总支出的比例。

blocks.html_en: At the same time, we are embarked upon a massive infrastructure spree, again of a kind not seen in decades: pipelines and electricity links and railways and more. Rather less has been done as yet on the productivity or internal trade barriers fronts, but these will surely have to follow – there is no way we will be able to pay for all this other spending if we don’t.

sentences.en: At the same time, we are embarked upon a massive infrastructure spree, again of a kind not seen in decades: pipelines and electricity links and railways and more.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们开始了大规模的基础设施建设热潮，这又是几十年来未见的：管道、电力线路、铁路等等。

sentences.en: Rather less has been done as yet on the productivity or internal trade barriers fronts, but these will surely have to follow – there is no way we will be able to pay for all this other spending if we don’t.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，在生产力或内部贸易壁垒方面所做的工作还较少，但这些肯定会随之而来——如果我们不这样做，我们将无法支付所有这些其他支出。

blocks.html_en: And we are beginning to be taken seriously again in international councils. Mark Carney’s personal reputation, as a former central banker and international financier, is only part of this. The reason his speech at Davos, calling on middle powers to get out from under the “hegemons’” thumbs, landed with such enormous impact was not just who said it, or where, or when – at the height of the Greenland fiasco – but that it was a Prime Minister of Canada, of all places, saying it.

sentences.en: And we are beginning to be taken seriously again in international councils.
sentences.zh: 我们开始在国际理事会中再次受到认真对待。

sentences.en: Mark Carney’s personal reputation, as a former central banker and international financier, is only part of this.
sentences.zh: 马克·卡尼作为前央行行长和国际金融家的个人声誉只是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: The reason his speech at Davos, calling on middle powers to get out from under the “hegemons’” thumbs, landed with such enormous impact was not just who said it, or where, or when – at the height of the Greenland fiasco – but that it was a Prime Minister of Canada, of all places, saying it.
sentences.zh: 他在达沃斯的演讲呼吁中等强国摆脱“霸权”的控制，之所以能产生如此巨大的影响，不仅仅是因为这句话是谁说的、在什么地方、什么时候说的——在格陵兰岛惨败最严重的时候——而是因为说这句话的人是加拿大总理。

blocks.html_en: This wasn’t Canada preaching from the sidelines. This was a politician with skin in the game, leading a country that was more dependent on one particular hegemon than any of the others represented there – and therefore more at risk. As a consequence, we are taking an outsized role in the construction of a post-American world.

sentences.en: This wasn’t Canada preaching from the sidelines.
sentences.zh: 这不是加拿大在场外说教。

sentences.en: This was a politician with skin in the game, leading a country that was more dependent on one particular hegemon than any of the others represented there – and therefore more at risk.
sentences.zh: 这是一位利益攸关的政治家，他所领导的国家比任何其他霸权国家都更加依赖某个霸权 — — 因此面临的风险也更大。

sentences.en: As a consequence, we are taking an outsized role in the construction of a post-American world.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在后美国世界的建设中发挥着巨大的作用。

blocks.html_en: Perhaps the most startling, and sudden, transformation has been our approach to energy development. The Prime Minister’s remarkable “forward guidance” video the other day amounted to a blunt disavowal of the last 10 years of Liberal policy. His reasoning was simple. The world has changed. New threats crowd upon us, that were not anticipated a decade ago, and new priorities must take their place alongside the fight against climate change. Government is about triage.

sentences.en: Perhaps the most startling, and sudden, transformation has been our approach to energy development.
sentences.zh: 也许最令人吃惊、最突然的转变是我们的能源开发方式。

sentences.en: The Prime Minister’s remarkable “forward guidance” video the other day amounted to a blunt disavowal of the last 10 years of Liberal policy.
sentences.zh: 前几天，首相出色的“前瞻性指导”视频直截了当地否认了过去十年的自由党政策。

sentences.en: His reasoning was simple.
sentences.zh: 他的理由很简单。

sentences.en: The world has changed.
sentences.zh: 世界已经改变。

sentences.en: New threats crowd upon us, that were not anticipated a decade ago, and new priorities must take their place alongside the fight against climate change.
sentences.zh: 新的威胁向我们袭来，这是十年前没有预料到的，在应对气候变化的同时，必须采取新的优先事项。

sentences.en: Government is about triage.
sentences.zh: 政府是关于分类的。

blocks.html_en: But it isn’t only Justin Trudeau’s legacy Mr. Carney has been busy overturning, for good or ill. It’s Pierre Trudeau’s. Mr. Carney is in many ways a throwback to a pre-Trudeau kind of Liberal. In style and tone, but even more in policy, he recalls the Liberals of the Lester Pearson era, and even more that of Louis St. Laurent: sober, bankerly, business-oriented, pro-development and pro-military.

sentences.en: But it isn’t only Justin Trudeau’s legacy Mr. Carney has been busy overturning, for good or ill.
sentences.zh: 但无论好坏，卡尼先生忙着推翻的不仅仅是贾斯汀·特鲁多的遗产。

sentences.en: It’s Pierre Trudeau’s.
sentences.zh: 这是皮埃尔·特鲁多的。

sentences.en: Mr. Carney is in many ways a throwback to a pre-Trudeau kind of Liberal.
sentences.zh: 卡尼先生在很多方面都是特鲁多之前的自由党的倒退。

sentences.en: In style and tone, but even more in policy, he recalls the Liberals of the Lester Pearson era, and even more that of Louis St. Laurent: sober, bankerly, business-oriented, pro-development and pro-military.
sentences.zh: 在风格和语气上，但在政策上，他让人想起莱斯特·皮尔逊时代的自由党，甚至更多的是路易斯·圣洛朗的时代：冷静、银行家、以商业为导向、支持发展和支持军事。

blocks.html_en: We remember Pearson as the father of peacekeeping. We are less likely to remember him as the Cold Warrior who accepted nuclear missiles on Canadian soil, and who spent more than 3 per cent of GDP, on average, on defence.

sentences.en: We remember Pearson as the father of peacekeeping.
sentences.zh: 我们铭记皮尔逊是维和之父。

sentences.en: We are less likely to remember him as the Cold Warrior who accepted nuclear missiles on Canadian soil, and who spent more than 3 per cent of GDP, on average, on defence.
sentences.zh: 我们不太可能记得他是一位冷战战士，他在加拿大领土上接受了核导弹，平均将国内生产总值的 3% 以上用于国防。

blocks.html_en: It was the Diefenbaker Conservatives who objected to the missiles. At the time the Liberals were the continentalists of Canadian politics, seeing engagement with the U.S. as a necessary counterbalance to the imperial connection they were so anxious to be rid of. The Tories were the opposite: fond of the mother country, suspicious of the Yanks. Only much later did the roles reverse, after Britain ceased to be an issue.

sentences.en: It was the Diefenbaker Conservatives who objected to the missiles.
sentences.zh: 反对导弹的是迪芬贝克保守党。

sentences.en: At the time the Liberals were the continentalists of Canadian politics, seeing engagement with the U.S. as a necessary counterbalance to the imperial connection they were so anxious to be rid of.
sentences.zh: 当时，自由党是加拿大政坛的大陆主义者，他们认为与美国的接触是对他们急于摆脱的帝国联系的必要制衡。

sentences.en: The Tories were the opposite: fond of the mother country, suspicious of the Yanks.
sentences.zh: 保守党则相反：热爱祖国，怀疑美国佬。

sentences.en: Only much later did the roles reverse, after Britain ceased to be an issue.
sentences.zh: 直到很久以后，英国不再是一个问题之后，角色才发生逆转。

blocks.html_en: Mr. Carney is a continentalist, too – he just has a different continent in mind. But his ardent pursuit of the European connection is in the same counter-balancing mould, not only of Liberal leaders past, but of statesmen through the ages: calling the Old World back into our existence, to redress the balance of the New.

sentences.en: Mr. Carney is a continentalist, too – he just has a different continent in mind.
sentences.zh: 卡尼先生也是一位大陆主义者——他只是想到了一个不同的大陆。

sentences.en: But his ardent pursuit of the European connection is in the same counter-balancing mould, not only of Liberal leaders past, but of statesmen through the ages: calling the Old World back into our existence, to redress the balance of the New.
sentences.zh: 但他对欧洲联系的热切追求与过去的自由党领导人和历代政治家一样，都具有相同的平衡模式：召唤旧世界回到我们的存在中，以纠正新世界的平衡。

content_html_zh:
唐纳德·特朗普时代伟大民主国家的年度聚会已经获得了一定的…… 韵律。 在总统抵达之前举行的会议，当时一切都像往常一样，在具有相同广泛意识形态色彩的世界领导人之间举行：欢乐的公开会议，亲密的合影，紧急的边会。

然后是他到达那里后发生的事情，以及绝望的争先恐后地调和随之而来的混乱与之前平静的常态：坚持认为，从总统到达那一刻起，他嘴里冒出的疯狂洪流，破坏了其他与会者商定的一切 — — 更不用说几十年来确定的国际法 — — 事实上与其他与会者完全一致。

今年在土耳其安卡拉举行的北约峰会也不例外。 这次会议的目的是在与俄罗斯的战争中精心展示对乌克兰的支持，同时也同样精心展示欧洲对自身防务的承诺，所有这些都是为了向特朗普证明，北约 2025 年海牙会议上达成的协议——提高非美国国防开支以换取美国继续参与欧洲事务——实际上正在得到执行。

观点：北约峰会成功吗？ 这取决于你如何定义它

然后特朗普先生来了。 在峰会前的几个月里，他一直在攻击和嘲笑北约和北约个别领导人，特别是他们未能卷入伊朗战争 — — 这场灾难与北约或其核心任务无关。 在峰会上事情升级了。 特朗普再次要求归还格陵兰岛，呼吁抵制与西班牙的贸易，并威胁要从欧洲撤出所有美军，准备对伊朗重新宣战。

但当一切结束时，一切都应该是甜蜜和轻松的。 会后宣言坚称联盟成员根据北约创始条约第5条“铁定”相互保卫的承诺，提到“俄罗斯构成的长期威胁”，吹嘘欧洲盟国和加拿大去年在核心国防需求上增加了1390亿美元的支出，并承诺盟国“坚定不移地支持乌克兰”。

就特朗普而言，他似乎很高兴，尤其是其他领导人对他的奉承，他将其视为爱。 “他们说，‘我们爱，先生，我们爱你。’ 这些都是成年人说的，这不是很好吗？ …… 我从来没有见过这样的东西。 这些国家中的每一个国家都爱我们，他们彼此相爱。” 不管它是什么，它似乎起作用了。 特朗普甚至承诺授权乌克兰制造美国爱国者防空系统。

当然，在大多数北约峰会上，第五条仍然完好无损，美国仍然参与其中，或者北约将俄罗斯视为威胁，这些都不会成为新闻。 但那是在特朗普出现在世界舞台之前。 这次会议可能成功地掩盖了联盟中的深刻裂痕，但没有人认真对待特朗普的承诺。 对第五条的考验不是北约伙伴现在对此的言论，而是他们在遭受攻击时的做法。

英国首相马克·卡尼表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统心情愉快地抵达北约，该联盟正在将军事预算负担从美国手中转移出去。

加拿大新闻社

如果说现在人们对美国保卫其盟友的意愿存在深刻怀疑，那就太轻描淡写了。 如果说北约内部几乎完全肯定不会这样做，那仍然是轻描淡写。 毕竟，最近对北约成员国领土完整的严重威胁并非来自俄罗斯。 它来自美国，而且来自美国：越过格陵兰岛。 它仍然徘徊在加拿大上空。

《华尔街日报》本周再次引发了对去年首次报道的一次对话的争议，据称特朗普在与总理贾斯汀·特鲁多的电话中威胁要废除界定美国和加拿大边界的 1908 年条约。 据报道，特朗普告诉特鲁多：“我把它撕了，你的整个国家就会崩溃。”

无论特朗普的好战性可能在多大程度上改变了与北约其他国家的关系，但与它改变与加拿大的关系并随之改变加拿大的关系相比，这根本算不了什么。 自 1867 年以来，我们从未认真考虑过美国总统可能试图以某种方式夺取我们部分领土的前景。

恰恰相反。 美国成为我们的恩人：我们最大的贸易伙伴、最亲密的盟友和军事保护者。 没有任何一个主要民主国家在贸易方面比另一个国家更加依赖，也没有任何其他国家在国防方面如此依赖另一个国家。

加拿大将两者结合起来，不仅衡量了我们对美国的依赖程度，而且还衡量了我们对现在所处的世界准备得多么不足——在这个世界中，我们不仅不能依赖美国进行国防，而且必须准备好保护自己免受美国的侵害。

然而，必须说的是，加拿大在这个世界上也有机会。 躲藏在美国贸易和国防轨道内有很多好处——确保进入美国市场、免受外部侵略——但也在很多方面让我们变得幼稚。

它让我们相信，我们不仅不需要为自己的防御付出代价，而且我们没有必要保卫自己——我们没有天敌。 它削弱了我们的竞争优势，导致我们忽视了我们的生产力——当我们总能把商品运往南方时，为什么要关心这些事情呢？

它让我们沉迷于自我毁灭的行为，比如对自己施加数百个省际贸易壁垒，或者沉溺于从一个或另一个省分裂的周期性威胁。 它使我们能够依赖脆弱的东西向交通和通讯联系，这使我们比我们必须认真对待破坏或其他强制性措施的威胁更容易受到伤害。

它鼓励了我们大多数加拿大人的消遣，向他人宣讲与我们没有直接关系的事情，基于我们没有赢得的优越美德的主张——当涉及到我们臭名昭著的北约贪图便宜时，这尤其令人恼火，但更普遍的是，这种自命不凡的倾向使我们被置于国际事务的边缘。

所有这一切都即将改变——已经在改变。 我们被迫同时在许多方面改变方向，这是至少过去 40 年来（也许是自 1945 年以来，也许是有史以来）对我们的前景和方向最彻底的重新评估。

卡尼在峰会上表示，特朗普在北约国防开支问题上“赢得了争论”

我们正试图将我们的部分贸易转向美国以外的其他国家，包括通过一系列全面的自由贸易协定，同时将我们的国防开支提高到自 1960 年代初以来未见的水平，无论是占 GDP 的比例还是占政府总支出的比例。

与此同时，我们开始了大规模的基础设施建设热潮，这又是几十年来未见的：管道、电力线路、铁路等等。 迄今为止，在生产力或内部贸易壁垒方面所做的工作还较少，但这些肯定会随之而来——如果我们不这样做，我们将无法支付所有这些其他支出。

我们开始在国际理事会中再次受到认真对待。 马克·卡尼作为前央行行长和国际金融家的个人声誉只是其中的一部分。 他在达沃斯的演讲呼吁中等强国摆脱“霸权”的控制，之所以能产生如此巨大的影响，不仅仅是因为这句话是谁说的、在什么地方、什么时候说的——在格陵兰岛惨败最严重的时候——而是因为说这句话的人是加拿大总理。

这不是加拿大在场外说教。 这是一位利益攸关的政治家，他所领导的国家比任何其他霸权国家都更加依赖某个霸权 — — 因此面临的风险也更大。 因此，我们在后美国世界的建设中发挥着巨大的作用。

也许最令人吃惊、最突然的转变是我们的能源开发方式。 前几天，首相出色的“前瞻性指导”视频直截了当地否认了过去十年的自由党政策。 他的理由很简单。 世界已经改变。 新的威胁向我们袭来，这是十年前没有预料到的，在应对气候变化的同时，必须采取新的优先事项。 政府是关于分类的。

但无论好坏，卡尼先生忙着推翻的不仅仅是贾斯汀·特鲁多的遗产。 这是皮埃尔·特鲁多的。 卡尼先生在很多方面都是特鲁多之前的自由党的倒退。 在风格和语气上，但在政策上，他让人想起莱斯特·皮尔逊时代的自由党，甚至更多的是路易斯·圣洛朗的时代：冷静、银行家、以商业为导向、支持发展和支持军事。

我们铭记皮尔逊是维和之父。 我们不太可能记得他是一位冷战战士，他在加拿大领土上接受了核导弹，平均将国内生产总值的 3% 以上用于国防。

反对导弹的是迪芬贝克保守党。 当时，自由党是加拿大政坛的大陆主义者，他们认为与美国的接触是对他们急于摆脱的帝国联系的必要制衡。 保守党则相反：热爱祖国，怀疑美国佬。 直到很久以后，英国不再是一个问题之后，角色才发生逆转。

卡尼先生也是一位大陆主义者——他只是想到了一个不同的大陆。 但他对欧洲联系的热切追求与过去的自由党领导人和历代政治家一样，都具有相同的平衡模式：召唤旧世界回到我们的存在中，以纠正新世界的平衡。
